root_cause: The legacy metadata selection flow imported the historical snapshot module and created a second hash-bearing runtime KnowledgeSnapshot before the canonical KnowledgeRetriever created its ArtifactEnvelope[domain.KnowledgeSnapshot]. This created two competing snapshot lifecycles in one vNext retrieval path.

alternatives_considered.option: Keep the legacy snapshot creation and label it as a cache.
alternatives_considered.reason: A hash-bearing cache created in the live retrieval path still competes with the canonical sealed snapshot and violates the single-authority boundary.

alternatives_considered.option: Remove the legacy module and break historical callers.
alternatives_considered.reason: The construction protocol permits a read-only compatibility adapter; historical replay callers remain supported without granting it vNext authority.

alternatives_considered.option: Move canonical snapshot construction into the legacy flow.
alternatives_considered.reason: The service owns K1/K2 gating, canonical candidate accounting, blocking-commit binding, and ArtifactEnvelope sealing. Moving that boundary back to the adapter would invert the architecture.

repair: knowledge_flow no longer imports knowledge_snapshot or creates a KnowledgeSnapshot. It now emits a sealed KnowledgeSelectionReceipt containing only bounded selection metadata for compatibility callers.
KnowledgeRetrievalResult exposes selection_receipt as its real field and retains snapshot only as a deprecated read-only compatibility property.

knowledge_snapshot no longer declares a KnowledgeSnapshot class. Its historical archive record is explicitly named LegacyKnowledgeSelectionArchive; the retired constructor name is resolved only through module-level compatibility lookup.

KnowledgeRetriever remains the sole vNext runtime owner that creates domain.KnowledgeSnapshot and seals it in ArtifactEnvelope. Its dependency trail records the adapter receipt, not a legacy snapshot authority.

checks.name: single_k1_k2_implementation
checks.evidence: A3 tests prove K1/K2 use the canonical KnowledgeStage, K2 requires a verified BlockingCommit, the service re-exports canonical types, the legacy flow has no snapshot-module import, and the compatibility module declares no second KnowledgeSnapshot class.

checks.name: replayable_snapshot
checks.evidence: A3 tests prove the sole runtime snapshot is ArtifactEnvelope[domain.KnowledgeSnapshot], accounts for every candidate, and fails closed on envelope tampering. Historical callers can replay only the bounded non-authoritative selection receipt without a search.

checks.name: untrusted_text_isolation
checks.evidence: The A3 quarantine test and legacy retrieval regression confirm raw untrusted source text and source IDs are excluded from Director-visible packet, receipt, and canonical snapshot.

checks.name: director_conflict_ownership
checks.evidence: A3 tests confirm conflict options remain exposed for Director resolution and are never auto-selected into the decision view.

checks.name: evidence_gated_promotion
checks.evidence: A3 tests confirm promotion rejects missing verified evidence, human approval, or any required observation-to-applicability chain component.

informational_results.name: workspace_delta_check
informational_results.command: git diff --check; static search for legacy snapshot import/class authority
informational_results.result: No whitespace errors; no legacy snapshot import in knowledge_flow; no KnowledgeSnapshot class declaration in compatibility module.

residual_risk: The historical adapter remains intentionally available for pre-vNext callers, but it is no longer on the canonical snapshot authority path. It cannot create K1/K2 authority, enter the Director view, or replace ArtifactEnvelope sealing.
